docs.title: Coriolis
docs.text:
Abstract

Coriolis supports migration of workloads between clouds and virtualization platforms. Its repository family separates the core product, container packaging, deployment delivery, and continuous-integration responsibilities.

docs.title: How The Repositories Work Together
docs.text:
These repositories have different relationships; they are not a simple dependency graph. coriolis-oss supplies core Coriolis source that coriolis-docker can use while building service images. Other product repositories also contribute where needed.

Runtime call hierarchy:
coriolis-ci
  -> coriolis-cd
       -> coriolis-docker
            -> Coriolis services and dependencies

Artifact progression:
Coriolis source -> container images and services -> appliance -> CI migration validation

coriolis-ci is Jenkins orchestration that invokes the coriolis-cd appliance delivery and deployment CLI. In turn, that CLI invokes coriolis-docker to build or deploy Coriolis service containers and their dependencies. coriolis-cd can also be used independently of CI.

docs.title: coriolis-oss
docs.text: The open-source Coriolis product source repository. It contains the API, migration workflows, workers, schedulers, provider integrations, and control-plane services that perform and manage migrations.

docs.title: coriolis-docker
docs.text: Deployment automation for Coriolis. It builds container images, deploys Coriolis services, and deploys their dependencies. See discovery. It uses upstream OpenStack Kolla and Kolla-Ansible for selected supporting services: Keystone, Barbican, RabbitMQ, and MariaDB. This is not a general-purpose OpenStack cloud deployment.

docs.title: coriolis-cd
docs.text: Appliance lifecycle and delivery tooling. Its CLI builds Coriolis components into appliance machines, deploys appliances, and supports appliance export, import, and test-machine operations.

docs.title: coriolis-ci
docs.text: Jenkins-based continuous integration. It provisions and configures appliances, deploys product components, runs migration tests, and collects results from complete workflows.

docs.title: Kubernetes And Helm
docs.text: No Kubernetes or Helm deployment support was found for the Coriolis product. The Helm chart at this repository's root deploys only this MkDocs documentation site.

docs.title: Auxiliary Client
docs.text: python-coriolismetalhubclient is an auxiliary Python client for bare-metal and Metal Hub integrations.

docs.title: Coriolis Discovery
docs.text:
Abstract

This in-progress map records observed product boundaries, delivery paths, and unresolved questions. It is not a deployment tutorial or finalized architecture.

docs.title: Repository Landscape
docs.text:
• coriolis-oss is the core application source.
  • coriolis-docker provides build and deployment automation.
  • coriolis-cd provides appliance delivery and deployment CLI tooling.
  • coriolis-ci is the Jenkins orchestrator and validation layer.
  • python-coriolismetalhubclient is an auxiliary client.

This root repository hosts the MkDocs site and its Helm chart only. That chart is not product Helm support.

docs.title: Observed Relationships
docs.text: coriolis-ci invokes coriolis-cd; coriolis-cd invokes Docker tooling on an appliance; and coriolis-docker builds or deploys services. coriolis-oss is a source input to those builds. These relationships are not a simple linear dependency graph: repositories can be used independently and additional sources contribute to individual images.

docs.title: Deployment Model
docs.text: The observed application deployment model uses Docker and Ansible. Selected OpenStack supporting services are deployed by upstream Kolla and Kolla-Ansible: Keystone, Barbican, RabbitMQ, MariaDB, and Memcached. No product Helm or Kubernetes deployment artifacts were found.

docs.title: Coriolis Images
docs.text: Coriolis-owned images share the coriolis-common base where applicable. Worker packages incorporate provider modules. The common image bundles the private replicator and writer. Application image registry and tags are configurable, but observed defaults are mutable.

docs.title: External Inputs
docs.text: Observed public base and runtime inputs include Ubuntu, Go, Node, Step CA, and InfluxDB. Kolla is a separate dependency image family rather than a Coriolis-owned application image family; its exact official public image mapping remains unresolved.

docs.title: Investigation Target
docs.text: The current intended deployment investigation targets a single Ubuntu 22.04 VM as a standard web appliance, with an OpenStack-to-OpenStack test migration and no Jenkins pipeline. The working assumption is a private registry for internally built Coriolis images and direct public pulls for public images. This is an investigation target, not a verified deployment recipe.

docs.title: Confirmed Gaps And Blockers
docs.text:
• Kolla version/tag alignment conflicts, and the exact public Kolla image list, remain unresolved.
  • The private dependency closure is incomplete.
  • coriolis_provider_vhi is referenced, but no source location was identified.
  • The worker build unconditionally clones the Metal Hub client.
  • libqemu binary provenance is unresolved.
  • Logger Dockerfile behavior needs validation.
  • No public or community deployment artifact was found.
  • Source and image references lack immutable pinning.
  • No host sizing has been recorded.
  • Endpoint, DNS, TLS, and registry image availability remain decisions or audits.

docs.title: Next Discovery Gates
docs.text:
1. Confirm private source access and required commits.
  2. Locate the coriolis_provider_vhi source.
  3. Align the Kolla release and identify the exact required images.
  4. Audit registry images, tags or digests, and entrypoints.
  5. Establish third-party and binary provenance.
  6. Perform a first controlled installation and migration test.

docs.title: Clone conductor repository
docs.text:
git clone git@github.com:virtomat/ci-test-repo.git virt-ci-test-repo
Initial directory structure should look like this: (expand to see) 
radu@ThinkPad-L380$ tree -L 2
.
├── docs
│    ├── README.md
│    └── test.md
├── helm
│    ├── Chart.yaml
│    ├── templates
│    │    ├── deployment.yaml
│    │    ├── ingress.yaml
│    │    └── service.yaml

├── app.py
├── Dockerfile
├── logger.py
├── README.md

docs.title: Docker Image
docs.text:
You can build the image with (local usage): 

docker build . -t testapp

Note

As this repo is integrated on the CI pipeline, there is no need to push the image Building the image locally is for testing purposes when (for some reason) the build fails.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Create regcred docker registry secret. This has to have Read permission over virtomat project (to pull cixpress images) and Read/Write permissions over target project. 

kubectl -n cixpress create secret docker-registry regcred \
           --docker-server=cr.virtomat.io \
           --docker-username='robot-virtomat+cixpress' \
           --docker-password='07NESZAGTyubvOW2aIOTHMBVlxuTGZ3o'

docs.title: Installation (Dev Cluster)
docs.text:
From source code repository(for reference only): 

helm install testapp ./helm
From published helm chart: 
helm install testapp oci://cr.virtomat.io/virtomat/cixpress/helm/testapp

Note

As this chart is integrated on the CD pipeline, there is no need to install it manually. CD is managed with ArgoCD

docs.title: Installation (Local Dev Cluster)
docs.text:
helm -n cixpress install conductor ./helm \
          --set logging=DEBUG \
          --set ingress.enableTLS=false \
          --set persistence.mount_dev_dir=true \
          --set dev_dir_path=/home/radu/Dev/virt-ci-test-repo

helm -n cixpress install conductor oci://cr.virtomat.io/virtomat/cixpress/helm/conductor \
          --set logging=DEBUG \
          --set ingress.enableTLS=false \
          --set persistence.mount_dev_dir=true \
          --set dev_dir_path=/home/radu/Dev/virt-ci-test-repo

Mounting local workdir inside the runtime container

Mounting local workdir inside the runtime container allows live modifications (in your IDE of choice) and reloads of the application runtime without any workarounds. This requires a working local microk8s cluster

Proxy-forward webhook calls from github

Proxy-forward webhook calls from github to local environment (https://www.ultrahook.com/) 

ultrahook conductor http://ci.dev.virtomat.io/conductor/start-build-pipeline

docs.title: Verify the installation
docs.text:
Check that the pods are fine (running and ready): 

radu@ThinkPad-L380$ kubectl -n cixpress get pods
NAME                                  READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
testapp-59c797ffbd-vhwn9              1/1     Running   0          70d

Note

Depending on the specific release name you used with helm install the name of the pods might have different names.

Check the ingress for the frontend and for the backend: 

03:32 PM ~
radu@ThinkPad-L380$ kubectl -n cixpress get ing
NAME            CLASS   HOSTS                   ADDRESS         PORTS     AGE
testapp-demo    nginx   testapp.virtomat.dev    85.204.43.218   80, 443   235d

docs.title: Project template
docs.text:
Info

I'm using a simple python app for test in this exercise. You can clone the source code from git@github.com:virtomat/ci-test-repo.git

Regardless of the language (python, java, Angular, etc) the project structure is the same. It looks like this:

radu@ThinkPad-L380$ tree -L 2
.
├── docs
│    ├── build_and_deploy.md
│    └── configuration.md
├── helm
│    ├── Chart.yaml
│    ├── templates
│    │    ├── deployment.yaml
│    │    ├── ingress.yaml
│    │    └── service.yaml
│    └── values.yaml
├── app.py
├── logger.py
├── Dockerfile
├── requirements.txt
└── README.md
  • docs - This is a directory dedicated for documentation related to this app. It is usually automatically build to a static html site with mkdocs.
  • helm - This is the Helm Chart definition. Notice the templates directory. A basic setup will require a deployment (the actual container in a pod), a service (expose the pod on the internal network) and an ingress (basic layer 7 routing rules, to expose the app outside the cluster)
  • app.py - Test app code (Flask app)
  • logger.py- Some logging setup I find useful.
  • Dockerfile - Dockerfile to build the container
  • README.md - Optional Readme file (deprecated in favor of docs directory).

docs.title: Pipeline templates
docs.text:
A pipeline template is pretty basic at this point (expected to be extended in functionality), and only specifies the steps in the pipeline. The definition is supported as json content and we use REST API to push and pull the template definitions.

For the Default template the json looks like this: 

{
  "Default": {
    "pvc": {
      "required": true,
      "size": "1Gi"
    },
    "steps": [
      {
        "icon": "feather:github",
        "name": "git-clone"
      },
      {
        "icon": "docker_decolorize",
        "name": "kaniko-build"
      },
      {
        "icon": "helm",
        "name": "helm-update"
      },
      {
        "icon": "heroicons_mini:arrow-path-rounded-square",
        "name": "cleanup"
      }
    ]
  }
}

  • pvc - This is the spec for a volume where the workspace will be. All steps in the pipeline will share this workspace.
  • steps - This are the steps in the pipeline. The execution will follow the order specified here. The naming is also important, as each step name becomed the prefix in finding the right manifest for the job.
Create/Update a template definition: (expand to see) 
curl --location 'http://ci.virtomat.dev/conductor/templates' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data '{
    "Default": {
        "pvc": {
            "required": true,
            "size": "1Gi"
        },
        "steps": [
            {
                "name": "git-clone",
                "icon": "feather:github"
            },
            {
                "name": "kaniko-build",
                "icon": "docker_decolorize"
            },
            {
                "name": "helm-update",
                "icon": "helm"
            },
            {
                "name": "cleanup",
                "icon": "heroicons_mini:arrow-path-rounded-square"
            }
        ]
    }
}'
Retrieve a template definition (expand to see) 
curl --location 'https://ci.virtomat.dev/conductor/templates'
{
    "Default": {
        "pvc": {
            "required": true,
            "size": "1Gi"
        },
        "steps": [
            {
                "icon": "feather:github",
                "name": "git-clone"
            },
            {
                "icon": "docker_decolorize",
                "name": "kaniko-build"
            },
            {
                "icon": "helm",
                "name": "helm-update"
            },
            {
                "icon": "heroicons_mini:arrow-path-rounded-square",
                "name": "cleanup"
            }
        ]
    }
}

Note

You can have as many templates as you want. Each template defines a new kind of pipeline.

docs.title: Pipeline configs
docs.text:
For the test app the json looks like this: 

{
  "templateName": "Default",
  "steps": {
    "git-clone": {
      "git_repo_url": "gitlab.com/virtomat/ci-test-repo.git",
      "git_branch": "main",
      "logging": "DEBUG",
      "webhook_secret": "4F2XqXXk",
      "ttlSecondsAfterFinished": 120
    },
    "kaniko-build": {
      "logging": "DEBUG",
      "ttlSecondsAfterFinished": 120
    },
    "helm-update": {
      "logging": "DEBUG",
      "ttlSecondsAfterFinished": 120
    },
    "cleanup": {
      "logging": "DEBUG",
      "docs_repo_url": "https://github.com/virtomat/voyager-docs.git",
      "ttlSecondsAfterFinished": 120
    }
  }
}

  • templateName - references the template name (it has to exist)
  • steps - The steps in the pipeline must follow the naming in the template.
    • git-clone - This step will clone the git repo in the workspace directory.
    • kaniko-build - This is the build steps (builds the container and pushes it to the registry)
    • helm-update - This is the helm update step (version increment) and published the Chart to registry
    • cleanup - Some cleanup tasks.

Todo

We should move ttlSecondsAfterFinished to template, this is a common config, usually applicable for all pipelines of the same kind

Curl call example (exand to see) 
curl --location 'http://ci.virtomat.dev/conductor/configure' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data '[

        "templateName": "Default",
        "steps": {
            "git-clone": {
                "git_repo_url": "gitlab.com/virtomat/ci-test-repo.git",

docs.title: Simulating github trigger
docs.text:
You can use a curl call to trigger a pipeline (just replace the repo url with your own repo url):

GitHub trigger (expand to see) 
curl --location 'https://ci.virtomat.dev/conductor/githubTrigger' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data '{
    "ref": "refs/heads/main",  
    "repository": {
        "clone_url": "https://github.com/virtomat/ci-test-repo.git"  
    }
}'
GitLab trigger (expand to see) 
curl --location 'https://ci.virtomat.dev/conductor/gitlabTrigger' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data '{
    "ref": "refs/heads/main",
    "repository": {
        "git_http_url": "https://gitlab.com/virtomat/ci-test-repo.git"
    }
}'
